name: NGC 3073 (Hubble)
blurb: NGC 3073, a dwarf lenticular galaxy, seen by Hubble.
label: ngc3073-hubble
story: A small lenticular galaxy beside the starburst spiral NGC 3079, which seems to be shaping it from afar. A wind driven by its big neighbor's starburst appears to be stripping its hydrogen gas into a cometary tail.

claims.text: NGC 3073 is a dwarf S0 (lenticular) galaxy and a companion of NGC 3079
Its cometary hydrogen tail is likely caused by ram-pressure stripping by NGC 3079's starburst-driven wind
Hubble imaged it in a program on globular clusters of low-luminosity elliptical galaxies in low-density environments
